_doc: Plain code/data patches applied by insert.py. 'patch': bytes written over the source ROM (orig asserted). 'vanilla': [start, end) ranges copied back from clean FireRed. Offsets are ROM offsets.

naming_vanilla.why: Use FireRed's own name-entry screen instead of the hack's Chinese one (pinyin page, misplaced entry line). The hack hooked DoNamingScreen/CB2_LoadNamingScreen to its screen at 0x9FF5EB4/0x9FF505C, swapped the first key handler, the text-entry box template and the controls text, and redrew the buttons in Chinese. Restored here. Kept from the hack: its extended template table (literal at NamingScreen_Init 0x9DB58 -> 0x9DE4EC4: number/phrase/password/category inputs, initialPage=upper), the u16 player-avatar gfx id (0x9EF68), translated titles. Its intro calls its own screen directly (bl at 0x9FF4214, out of BL range of vanilla), so its entry becomes an ARM trampoline to vanilla DoNamingScreen; r0-r3 and stack args untouched. DoNamingScreen (vanilla entry 0x9D954 and the hack's entry 0x9FF5EB4) now jumps to a dispatcher built by insert.py: templates 0-4 (player/box/nickname/rival) run FireRed's screen; the hack's own templates 5-9 (number/phrase/password/category) crash FireRed's screen, so they go to the hack's screen as before (its old hook stored r0 at [sp]).

vanilla_battle_text.why: Live vanilla battle strings the hack half-overwrote in place (broken 2-byte codes such as 07 FE, leftover English like '…with its opponent!', 的/是/果 suffixes the dump skips as single characters). Restored to FireRed's English; each range was checked to be untouched by our build.

naming_abc_default.why: Hack's own name-entry screen (still used for its number/phrase/password/category prompts): open on the ABC page instead of the pinyin page. Init (0x9FF505C) zeroes currentPage (struct+0x2622, sNamingScreen at 0x203998C); the keyboard draw (0x9FF5A00) loads page 0's tilemap and preloads page 1's. Select still cycles CHN -> symbols -> ABC.

patch.asm: r2=base+0x261A; strh 0,1,0 at +0x261A/C/E... (same stores as before) then 0x2620=0, page(0x2622)=2; ldr r1,=0x262C kept
patch._note: orig: ldr r2 / strh r3,[r0,r2] pairs for 0x261A..0x2622 (ldr r2,=0x261A at 0x1FF50A0 kept)

namebox_width.why: Dialogue name box: scripts set VAR 0x8000-0x8003 = x 2, y 12, width 6, height 2 tiles and callasm 0x08FB0001 (window). 6 tiles fit four hanzi; English names need more ('Mr. Pokémon' 65px). The hack itself uses width 8 once. All 84 width-6 setups -> 8 tiles (64px).

ability_popup_possessive.why: CFRU's PrintBattlerOnAbilityPopUp (0x1CEAAE4) appends the possessive to the battler's name as three bytes: movs r2,#3 / strb; adds r2,#8 / strb; adds r2,#0xF4 / strb = 03 0B FF, i.e. the hanzi 的 + terminator, shown as 'Zorua的' above the ability name. Immediates changed so it stores B4 E7 FF (apostrophe, 's', terminator): movs r2,#0xB4; adds r2,#0x33 (-> E7); adds r2,#0x18 (-> FF). Same length, nothing else touched (issue #6, PLAYTEST finding 17).

rival_icon_hack_sheet.why: FireRed's naming screen draws the rival's icon (NamingScreen_CreateRivalIcon 0x9F04C) from a sheet table at 0x3E23C0 / palette 0x3E23C8, but takes OAM/animations from object graphics entry 0. Mercury/CFRU made entry 0 a 32x32 sprite, so FireRed's 16x32 brown-haired rival sheet came out as four garbled fragments, and it is the wrong character anyway: the hack's rival is the red-haired one (object graphics entry 72: 9 frames x 512 B at 0x9F54D34, palette 0x9F55F34). Point the sheet and palette at those; entry 0's 32x32 shape then matches. The icon's walk-in-place loop (cmds at 0x3E23A8) addresses frames in tile units: 0, 24, 0, 32 = frames 0/3/0/4 of vanilla's 8-tile frames; the hack's frames are 16 tiles, so 24 and 32 become 48 and 64.

money_symbol_vanilla.why: Money sign: FireRed draws the Pokédollar at character 0xB7 (charmap '¥'), and the hack kept the character - the Mart's price list and the trainer card print it - but it redrew the glyph in its Latin font as the kanji 円, so English text shows 円 next to prices. Restore FireRed's glyph in the font the game uses. The blob holds two copies of the font: 0x1F5EC0 is the edited one the game draws with, 0x1F9EC0 is already vanilla. Larger Latin letters in this font sit one row higher than FireRed's, so the restored glyph is a touch taller than the hack's own letters - that is FireRed's own shape, which is what the report asked for.

unown_page_12._doc: Unown notes page 12 starts mid-string (0E3DB54) while page 11 shows the whole string from 0E3DB2F: English written so the tail from byte 37 reads as its own page (#100).

bag_list_buffer._doc: Bag list string buffer (#121): LoadBagItemListBuffers allocates 27 bytes per entry, but this hack's entry string is a 14-byte prefix + the item name + terminator, so a 13-letter English name needs 28 bytes. Slot k's spill is overwritten by slot k+1; only the LAST slot spills past the block, and when 27*count is a multiple of 4 (28 entries) it clobbers the next heap block header, the bag never finishes loading (Shuckle's feed list with 'Maranga Berry' last, black screen + static). The Alloc size computation 'r0=7n; r0<<=2; r0-=n' (27n) becomes 'r0=7n; r0<<=2; r0+=8' (28n+8); the slot stride stays 27.
